title: Where the closing delimiter sits

blocks.text: The page shows that the **closing** `"""` decides two things about a text block's value: whether it ends with a newline, and how much indentation is removed. Here you compute a value the way the compiler does.

Write `TextBlockValue.evaluate(String body)`. `body` is the source text that follows the opening `"""` and its line terminator, **up to and including the closing `"""`**. Content lines never contain a quote, a backslash, a tab, a blank line or trailing spaces. The value is found like this:

items:
Line terminators in the source (`
`, `
` or ``) all count as one line break, and the value uses `
` between lines.

If only spaces come before the closing `"""` on its line, the closing delimiter is **on its own line**: that line is not content, and the value ends with a newline after the last content line. Otherwise the text before `"""` is the last content line and the value has no newline after it.
The indentation removed from every content line is the smallest number of leading spaces among the content lines **and the closing delimiter's line** when it is on its own line.

headers: body (`·` is a space, `⏎` a line break)

cases.says: With the closing delimiter on the last content line, the smallest indentation of the lines is removed and no newline is added.
A closing delimiter on its own line ends the value with a newline.
A closing delimiter to the left of the content counts in the smallest indentation, so the content keeps the difference; at column 0 it keeps all of it.
A closing delimiter to the right of the content does not raise the removed indentation; it only takes part in a minimum.
A block with no content line, only the closing delimiter, is the empty string, with no newline.
Source saved with \r\n or \r line endings gives the same value, with \n between lines.

concepts: The closing delimiter's column takes part in the smallest indentation, so moving it left keeps indentation in the value.
A closing delimiter on its own line ends the value with a newline; on the last content line it adds none.
A text block with no content line is the empty string.
The compiler normalizes line terminators to \n, removes incidental whitespace, then interprets escapes.
